title: Sariputra's promise (Kern ch. 3)
hook: the wise Sariputra is told he too will become a Buddha

segments.voice: Yesterday, a father called his children out of a burning house with the promise of carts, and gave each the finest cart of all. Your line: out of the burning house. Did you start from what someone loves? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-five.

A sealed envelope sits on a desk. Inside is a letter about your future, written by someone who knows you better than you know yourself. Would you open it? Chapter three of the Lotus Sutra opens with a moment like that, though it happens out loud, in front of everyone. Before the burning house is ever told, the Buddha speaks to the disciple who has been asking all along, and tells him something he had stopped hoping to hear. Today: Sariputra's promise.
screen: `A SEALED ENVELOPE.` → `A LETTER ABOUT YOUR FUTURE.` → `READ ALOUD, IN FRONT OF EVERYONE.`

segments.voice: First, the joy. The chapter actually begins here, before the parable we heard yesterday. Sariputra stands, palms joined, glowing with happiness after what he heard in chapter two. In Kern's translation he tells the Buddha he had been troubled for a long time. Sitting alone, he would wonder why the bodhisattvas were promised Buddhahood and the disciples like him were not. He had thought it was his own fault. Now the doubt is gone. Second, the promise. The Buddha answers him in front of the whole assembly. Long ago, he says, I was already guiding you, though you had forgotten. And in a future age, after honoring many Buddhas and keeping the teaching, you yourself will become a Buddha. The sutra even gives the name: Padmaprabha, which can be rendered Lotus Light, with a land of his own, wide and well ordered. Third, why it lands so hard. Sariputra was not a beginner. In Buddhist memory he is the disciple known for wisdom, the one the Buddha had just chosen to speak to. If even he had been quietly carrying the fear of being left out, the promise speaks to anyone who has assumed the best things were meant for other people. Fourth, the pattern. It will not be the last such promise in the Lotus. Over the coming chapters, one disciple after another hears his future, and later women of the assembly hear theirs too. The one vehicle from two days ago is not left as a theory. It is said to a person, by name. Some readers in the Tiantai, Tendai and Nichiren traditions dwell on these scenes, because they make the teaching personal: every being, in this sutra's view, can wake up. And that includes the one who thought he'd missed his chance.
screen: `SARIPUTRA'S QUIET DOUBT.` · `YOU WILL BECOME A BUDDHA.` · `EVEN THE WISE ONE WAS AFRAID.` · `NOT THE LAST PROMISE.` · then, large: `HE TOO WILL WAKE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: picture someone's full potential. Sit, and let the breath settle. Bring to mind one person you know well, maybe someone you've quietly given up on, or someone who seems to have given up on themselves. See their face. Then let the picture widen: this same person, years from now, at their kindest, wisest, most awake. Don't argue with the picture. Just let it be there. Breathe with it. If your own face appears in the picture instead, let that be fine too. The bell holds the time.
Sariputra's promise. In chapter three of the Lotus, the wise disciple who feared he'd been left out is told by name that he too will become a Buddha. Today's word.
Your line: he too will wake. Today, say one sentence to someone about what you see them becoming, and mean it. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-five.

howItsDone: In Lotus Sutra study, especially in the Tiantai, Tendai and Nichiren schools, Sariputra's prediction in chapter three is read as opening the sutra's promises that disciples, and in time all beings, will become Buddhas.

fork.setup: you are Sariputra. for years you've quietly believed the highest awakening was for others, not you. the Buddha turns to you before everyone. what does he say?
options: that you were right, and should be content
that you will become a Buddha, and he names you
that you must wait for another life to ask
fork.reveal: he tells Sariputra that he will become the Buddha Padmaprabha, with a land of his own, and that he had been guiding him long before.

original.note: Sanskrit form of the name; in Pali, Sariputta, son of Sari, his mother.

trapdoor: what you thought: a reward for the star pupil.
what it means: the disciple who feared he was shut out is promised Buddhahood by name, the one vehicle made personal.
what a scholar hears: Sariputra's prediction (vyakarana) opens a chain of predictions running through the Lotus, applying the one-vehicle teaching to each hearer in turn.

notes: Chapter 3 opening paraphrased from Kern (SBE XXI, 1884); nothing quoted.

Check: Sariputra's confession of earlier doubt and self-blame; the Buddha's statement that he had guided Sariputra in the past; the name Padmaprabha and the rendering 'Lotus Light' (padma, lotus; prabha, light); Kern names the land (Viraga or similar) and the age; omitted here.
'The disciple known for wisdom' reflects the wider Pali tradition (foremost in wisdom); the claim is softened to avoid a superlative.
Original note: Sariputta, 'son of Sari', is the standard Pali explanation of the name; Keeper to confirm.
'Women of the assembly hear theirs too' anticipates day 1167 (Mahapajapati and Yasodhara); check it is accurate to Kern's chapter 12.
